S5.01.needs: a chat that already has messages
S5.01.note: The chat title is written in a screen-reader-only heading in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; I did not confirm a visible title text in the top bar.
steps: Sign in and click Chat in the left sidebar, then open a chat from Recents (or send a first message).
Look at the top bar of the chat page.
Click the Share button, then the chevron menu next to it, and check that the menu offers rename, move, share, print, export, branch and delete.
Compare with Expected: the top bar should show where you are and the main actions for this view.
S5.01.where: Open any chat that has messages, then look at the top bar (Share button and chevron menu at the top right)

S5.02.needs: none (Health appears only when a health space is available; Home | Code only when Code is enabled)
S5.02.note: The nav list is defined in apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts; Health is hidden unless requiresHealthSpace is met.
steps: Sign in; the left sidebar shows the nav rows.
Click Projects, then Library, then Sites, and watch the main area change.
Find the two-part switch with Home and Code (shown only when the Code option is enabled for the account) and click Code.
Compare with Expected: each click should move to that product area or mode.
S5.02.where: Sidebar > Chat, Projects, Library, Sites, Health, Study (nav rows); and the Home | Code switch above the chat list

S5.04.needs: a second workspace (a team/enterprise membership) for switching; a Free account shows only Personal
S5.04.note: The active workspace is not shown on the sidebar itself in the code I read; it appears only inside the Workspace submenu.
steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Hover or click Workspace.
Look at the list: Personal (detail Only you) and any Enterprise workspaces; the active one is marked with a check icon.
Click a different workspace, read the switch warning, and check that the app reloads in that workspace (Expected).
S5.04.where: Sidebar bottom > account button (Account menu for your name) > Workspace > Personal / Enterprise

S5.05.needs: a wide window (desktop width); on a phone the sidebar is a drawer instead
steps: Sign in on a wide window so the sidebar is open.
Click the Toggle sidebar button in the sidebar header (or press Cmd+B).
Check that the sidebar collapses to a narrow icon rail.
Click the same button again (or press Cmd+B) and check that the sidebar expands.
S5.05.where: Sidebar header > Toggle sidebar button (keyboard: Cmd+B on Mac, Ctrl+B on Windows)

S5.07.needs: at least one saved chat with a known title
S5.07.note: The sidebar search entry opens a search dialog (GlobalSearchDialog); it does not filter the sidebar list in place.
steps: Click Search in the sidebar, or press Cmd+Shift+F.
A search panel opens over the app.
Type part of a chat title that you know exists.
Compare with Expected: matching conversations should appear as results and open when clicked.
S5.07.where: Sidebar > Search (row with a Search icon, shortcut shown as Cmd+Shift+F, or Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows)

steps: From any page in the app, click New Chat at the top of the sidebar, or press Shift+Cmd+O.
Check that a blank chat opens with an empty message box.
Send a message, then click New Chat again and check that a second, fresh chat opens.
S5.08.where: Sidebar > New Chat button at the top of the sidebar (shortcut Shift+Cmd+O, or Shift+Ctrl+O on Windows)

steps: Hover a chat row in Recents and click its More options (three dots) button.
Click Pin.
Check that the chat moves into a section headed Pinned at the top of the list.
Click Unpin in the same menu and check that it returns to its date group.
S5.09.where: Sidebar > Pinned (section at the top of the chat list)

steps: Create two or more chats by sending a message in each.
Look at the list under the Recents heading.
Click an older chat and check that it opens with its messages.
Compare with Expected: recent conversations are listed and open on selection.
S5.10.where: Sidebar > Recents (heading above the chat list)

S5.11.needs: a project with at least one chat moved into it
steps: Move a chat into a project: hover the chat, click More options, then Move to project, and pick a project.
Hover the Recents heading and click the sliders icon named Organize chats.
With By project selected (the default), check that the moved chat appears under its project row and not in Recents.
Choose In one list and check that all chats appear in Recents again.
S5.11.where: Sidebar > Recents heading > Organize chats (sliders icon) > By project or In one list

S5.12.note: Expected says This week, but the code labels are Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days and Older; groups with no chats are not shown.
steps: Have chats from different days (or use an account with older chats).
Look at the group headings above the chat rows.
Click a heading to collapse or expand its group.
Compare with Expected: the headings should be Today, Yesterday, This week, Older.
Click a chat row in Recents.
Check that the chat opens in the main area with its title and messages.
Check that the row you clicked now has a highlighted background (it is marked as the current page).
Click a different row and check that the highlight moves.
S5.13.where: Sidebar > Recents > a chat row (click the title)

S5.14.note: The Projects section in the sidebar appears only once the account has at least one project.
steps: Click Projects in the sidebar nav, then New project and create one.
Go back to the sidebar and find the project under the Projects section.
Click the project name and check that the project page opens (address /chat/projects/ with the project id).
Hover the project row and check the New chat in project and More options buttons.

S5.15.needs: a Work task that already exists (how to start one was not confirmed in the code I read)
S5.15.note: The Work marker is a small dot (session.agiWork), not a separate label; how a Work task is started was not traced.
steps: Find a row in Recents that carries the Work marker (a small dot, no chat-style row).
Click the row and check that it opens the task.
Compare with Expected: the row should be visibly different from a plain chat and show its state.
For the full task list, open the command palette (Cmd+K) and choose Work history.
S5.15.where: Sidebar > Recents > a row marked Work (a small dot with the word Work for screen readers)

S5.16.needs: a chat and a project whose names match a word you type
S5.16.note: The icons are in the command palette; sidebar rows use a dot and a screen-reader word instead.
steps: Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows).
Type a word from a chat title and from a project name.
Look at each result row: it has an icon and a hidden type label (Chat, Project, File, Artifact and so on).
Compare with Expected: the type should be recognisable from the icon and announced for screen readers.
S5.16.where: Press Cmd+K > type a word > results show an icon and a type label for each row

S5.17.needs: an account that can send a message and get a reply
steps: Send a question that takes a while to answer in a chat.
While the reply is still coming in, look at the chat row in Recents.
Check that a pulsing dot appears beside the title.
When the reply finishes, check that the dot disappears.
S5.17.where: Sidebar > Recents > the chat row whose reply is still running

S5.18.needs: a run that is waiting for your approval or input
S5.18.note: The flag comes from server state (apps/web/lib/server/neon-chat.ts); there is no button that creates it, so the tester must trigger a run that waits.
steps: Start a run that asks you for approval or input (for example, a task that waits for you).
Leave the chat open or move to another chat.
Look at the chat row in Recents for an amber dot, and hover or inspect it for the word Needs you for screen readers.
Answer the question and check that the amber dot clears.
S5.18.where: Sidebar > Recents > a chat row with an amber dot

S5.19.note: I did not trace the code that clears the unread flag on open; the tester can confirm it by clicking.
steps: Hover a chat row in Recents, click More options, then Mark as unread.
Check that the row shows a blue dot and a bold title, and that the screen-reader text says Unread.
Click the row and check that the dot and bold title clear.
Compare with Expected: unread items are marked and clear when opened.
S5.19.where: Sidebar > Recents > chat row with a blue dot and bold title (set Mark as unread from More options)

S5.20.needs: at least one saved chat; a project for Move to project
S5.20.note: Share and Move to project appear only when the matching action is provided; the list in Expected matches the code.
steps: Hover a chat row in Recents and click More options.
Check the menu order: Share, Rename, Pin, Mark as unread, Archive, Delete, Move to project.
Use Move to project (when projects exist) and check that the chat moves.
Use Delete and check that a confirmation dialog appears before anything is removed.
S5.20.where: Sidebar > hover a chat row > More options (three dots)

S5.21.note: Clicking away from the field also saves the new title (blur calls submitRename), which Expected does not mention.
steps: Hover a chat row, click More options, then Rename.
The title turns into a text field: type a new name and press Enter.
Check that the new title shows in the row, then reload the page and check it is still there.
Start a rename again, press Escape, and check that the old title comes back.
S5.21.where: Sidebar > chat row > More options > Rename

S5.25.needs: the Electron desktop app for the menu; a browser for the browser's own back button
steps: Open two different chats, one after the other.
In the Electron desktop app, click History in the menu bar, then Back (shortcut Cmd+[).
Check that the earlier chat opens again.
Click History > Forward (Cmd+]) and check that the later chat returns.
S5.25.where: Menu bar > History > Back and Forward (desktop app only; in the browser use the browser's back and forward buttons)

S5.26.note: The palette is opened by the capture-phase listener in apps/web/shared/components/CommandPalette/CommandPaletteProvider.tsx.
steps: Press Cmd+K from any page.
Check that a dialog opens with the placeholder Search chats and actions.
Type settings and press Enter on Go to Settings.
Compare with Expected: the palette runs the command and opens that destination.
S5.26.where: Press Cmd+K anywhere (Ctrl+K on Windows) > command palette

steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar, then Get help, then Keyboard shortcuts.
Or press Cmd+/ (Ctrl+/ on Windows) from a chat page.
Check that a dialog titled Keyboard Shortcuts opens and lists the shortcuts with their keys.
Press Escape and check that the dialog closes.
S5.27.where: Account menu (bottom of sidebar) > Get help > Keyboard shortcuts (or press Cmd+/)

S5.28.needs: a notification (for example a finished run); an empty account shows the empty message
S5.28.note: The empty-state text is: When a run finishes, a report is ready or something needs you, it shows up here.
steps: Click the bell at the top of the sidebar.
Check the panel titled Notifications, with an unread count on the bell when there are unread items.
Click a notification row and check that it opens its target.
Click Mark all as read and check the unread dots clear and the count goes away.
S5.28.where: Sidebar top, next to the AGI wordmark > bell button (Notifications)

S5.29.note: The account menu is defined in apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx; the plan is shown as a badge on the footer, and Free accounts see a Free plan line with Upgrade.
steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Check that your email shows at the top of the menu.
Check the items: Workspace, Settings, Get help, Upgrade (only when offered), Log out.
Click Settings and check that the Settings page opens; then sign out with Log out and check you return to sign-in.
S5.29.where: Sidebar bottom > account button (Account menu for your name)

S5.30.note: Learn more, Data use, Data rights and Terms and policies are in a separate Learn more submenu of the same account menu.
steps: Click the account button at the bottom of the sidebar, then Get help.
Check the options: Get help, Email support, Send feedback, Keyboard shortcuts.
Click Send feedback and check that the feedback dialog opens.
Click Keyboard shortcuts and check that the shortcuts dialog opens.
S5.30.where: Account menu (bottom of sidebar) > Get help

S5.31.note: Code is partial: the owner-held billing waitlist (AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN, billing-waitlist-access.ts) decides whether Upgrade reaches checkout or the waitlist dialog, so the tester may see the waitlist instead of a plan flow.
steps: Sign in with a Free account and look at the bottom of the sidebar for the "Free plan" row.
Click the "Upgrade" button on that row.
Open the account menu from the sidebar and look for the "Upgrade" item (it is hidden when the plan has no self-serve upgrade path).

Click "Upgrade" and compare with Expected: an eligible user should reach the plan upgrade flow. Note that paid checkout is gated: while billing upgrades are closed, the flow shows the waitlist dialog instead of checkout.
S5.31.where: Sidebar account footer > "Free plan" row > Upgrade button; or the account menu ("Account menu for ..." in the sidebar) > Upgrade

S5.32.needs: a Mac with Wi-Fi that can be switched off, and a signed-in account
S5.32.note: The Retry button appears only in the error state (after a sync error), not while offline, so there is no reconnect control when the network is down; the code does not show a separate backend-connection indicator.
steps: Sign in and stay on any screen.
Turn off Wi-Fi on the Mac (or disconnect the network) and wait a few seconds.
Look for the status strip under the header: it should show a connection state such as "Offline".
Check whether a reconnect control is offered; compare with Expected (it should offer reconnect when not connected).
S5.32.where: Any screen > the status strip that drops in below the header (labelled "Network status indicator"); it appears on connection loss or a sync error, with no menu

S5.33.needs: a Mac with Wi-Fi that can be switched off, and a signed-in account; queued items show "pending" only if some work is waiting
S5.33.note: When back online the strip hides unless items are queued or syncing, so it clears rather than showing an "Online" message.
steps: Sign in and stay on any screen.
Turn off Wi-Fi on the Mac.
Look for the strip under the header showing "Offline" (with "pending" if changes are queued).
Turn Wi-Fi back on and wait; compare with Expected: the strip should clear once the app is back online.
S5.33.where: Any screen > turn off Wi-Fi; the status strip under the header appears; turn Wi-Fi back on

S5.34.needs: a Mac desktop build; to see the update-available or update-ready dialog a newer published version must exist (otherwise only the up-to-date dialog appears)
S5.34.note: The in-app check also exists as "Check for updates" in the Settings update row (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopUpdateRow.tsx) and a "Relaunch to update" banner (DesktopUpdateNotice.tsx); the Settings tab that holds that row was not confirmed.
steps: Click the app's own menu in the Mac menu bar.
Click "Check for Updates…".
Read the dialog: if you have the latest version it says the app is up to date; if a newer one exists it offers "Download Installer" (or "Relaunch to update" once downloaded).
Compare with Expected: the dialog should say whether a new release is available and how to get it.
S5.34.where: Menu bar > the app's own menu (the menu named after the app, far left, next to the Apple menu) > Check for Updates…

S5.35.note: The header button is an icon with an aria-label, so no visible word is shown on it; the code path is the compact tier (app-shell-layout.ts, SHELL_TABLET_MIN_WIDTH = 768).
steps: Drag the window edge until the window is narrower than about 768 px wide.
Click the menu icon at the top-left of the header (accessible name "Open navigation").
Look for the navigation drawer sliding in from the left, with the sidebar items inside.
Press Escape or click outside the drawer, then check it closes and keyboard focus returns to the menu button; compare with Expected.
S5.35.where: Resize the app window narrower than 768 px > header button at top-left labelled "Open navigation" > navigation drawer slides in from the left

S5.37.needs: a window that can be resized to tablet widths
S5.37.note: Code (app-shell-layout.ts) keeps the sidebar persistent in landscape but uses a rail that expands over the content in portrait, which is not the side-by-side layout Expected describes.
steps: Resize the window to between 768 and 1023 px wide with the window wider than tall (landscape).
Look: the navigation sidebar should stay beside the content (persistent).
Resize to a taller-than-wide (portrait) window at the same width.
Look: in portrait the sidebar shows only icons and expands over the content instead of sitting beside it; compare with Expected.
S5.37.where: Resize the window to a width from 768 px to 1023 px; the sidebar layout is chosen by width and orientation (no control)

S5.38.needs: a signed-in account with a notification that links to a chat or task
S5.38.note: Stable links use the path /open/<type>/<id> (packages/contracts/types/src/product-links.ts), and the desktop deep-link scheme is agiworkforce-cloud (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts); the bell's visible label was not confirmed, so the tester should locate it by icon.
steps: Make sure an account has a notification that points at a chat or a task.
Open the notifications bell from the sidebar header.
Click that notification.
Look: the app should open that chat or task directly, and the address should point at the item; compare with Expected.
S5.38.where: Sidebar > the bell icon next to the wordmark (notifications) > click a notification about a chat, project or task

S5.39.needs: a Free or paid account and a chat you can delete
S5.39.note: The loading screen is brief, so capture it on a slow connection; the unavailable copy also varies by reason (deleted, no access, not found).
steps: Delete a chat you own, or pick a link to a chat that no longer exists.
Open that link from the app (for example from a notification).
Look for the "Loading chat" screen while it resolves.
Look for the unavailable screen: a title such as "This chat isn’t available" with a "Back to chats" button; compare with Expected.
S5.39.where: Open a chat link whose chat was deleted (for example from a notification about it): the screen shows "Conversation not found"; the "Loading chat" screen appears while the chat resolves
